steps: Choose System and Follow App Appearance in Settings.
Change the actual OS color mode while Settings and an independent SQL tab remain open.
Observe application controls, SQL, retained preview, diagnostics and popup colors.
Choose Solarized Light for the application, change OS mode again and observe the named workbench palette remains active.
native_cases.persistence: OS changes reserve no appearance write.

steps: Choose Porter for application and JetBrains Light for editor.
Close normally immediately after the second choice.
Restart with original imported theme sources removed.
Observe independent committed choices, resolved palettes and disconnected restored SQL.
Inspect actual UIA or AT-SPI name, automation ID, value, disabled state, focus and actions.
Open with keyboard, navigate/filter, commit with Enter, dismiss with Escape, Tab through controls and Done.
Repeat at supported DPI and mixed monitor scales under opposite app/editor colors.
native_cases.evidence: Record real target properties; headless element IDs are not native acceptance.

steps: Use only an isolated owned test data directory.
Start with corrupt/future/duplicate-key appearance bytes, then open Settings.
Preview colors and close without edits or after preview-only edits. Verify original bytes remain unchanged and close succeeds.
Externally repair the file and explicitly Reload Saved Settings.
Verify the current preview is replaced and only later accepted changes may save.
Rapidly alternate both selectors while retaining a running SQL operation and grid selection.
Inject supported isolated file-write failure or external conflict.
Observe fixed error, preview, Retry Saving or explicit Reload.
Close normally while the latest save is pending; only latest Published authorizes final removal.
Cancel close before completion and verify original SQL, helper/session/transaction and other owners remain retained.
